gate: Article XX — Problem existence is a gate before mechanism optimization
ceo_directive: Do not substitute generic VP-shunt obstruction evidence for eShunt evidence.
epistemic_state: YELLOW — plausible but not yet observed in eShunt-specific clinical data

NCT05232838.description: US Pilot Study of the CereVasc eShunt System in Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus
NCT05232838.epistemic_class: MANUFACTURER_REPORTED — primary clinical trial data (not yet peer-reviewed at time of search)

NCT06498960_STRIDE.description: STRIDE — Prospective, multi-center, randomized, controlled trial of the eShunt System in NPH
NCT06498960_STRIDE.adverse_event_reporting: All adverse events reported through 6 months post-procedure
NCT06498960_STRIDE.follow_up: 1 year primary, up to 5 years focused care
NCT06498960_STRIDE.status: Enrollment complete (Jan 2026 per ETCHES); pivotal trial for FDA approval

jnis_2026_publication.description: Safety of endovascular shunting for normal pressure hydrocephalus (multi-center study)
jnis_2026_publication.comparison: comparable to 3-month improvement rates after VP shunt
jnis_2026_publication.epistemic_class: PEER_REVIEWED — published in Journal of NeuroInterventional Surgery

cerevasc_own_positioning.claim: eShunt Implant is intended to significantly reduce failures associated with VPS systems such as infection, catheter obstruction, and over-drainage.
cerevasc_own_positioning.interpretation: CereVasc explicitly acknowledges obstruction as a VP-shunt failure mode that eShunt is designed to reduce. This is a MARKETING CLAIM, not yet a clinical fact. The device is investigational.

maude_status.finding: No eShunt-specific MAUDE reports found. eShunt is investigational (not yet FDA-approved for commercial sale). Adverse events for IDE devices are reported directly to FDA as part of the IDE trial, NOT to MAUDE.
maude_status.epistemic_class: ABSENCE_OF_EVIDENCE — per Article XXV, this is NOT evidence that no adverse events exist. It is evidence that the device is not yet in MAUDE's scope.
maude_status.implication: Post-market surveillance data will NOT be available until after FDA approval and commercialization. The problem-existence gate must rely on clinical trial data + anatomical analogy, not MAUDE.

ventriculoatrial_shunt_VA.anatomy: CSF drained from ventricle to right atrium via distal catheter in the venous system
ventriculoatrial_shunt_VA.analogous_to_eshunt_because: Both drain CSF into the venous system. Both have a blood-device interface at the venous end.

thrombosis_evidence.source: Wu 2022 (Child's Nervous System, PMID via PMC8976808), J Neurosurg Pediatrics 2(4):p286

ventriculoatrial_shunt_VA.epistemic_class: INDEPENDENT_PEER_REVIEWED — strong evidence that venous-side CSF drainage has significant thrombosis risk

ventriculosinus_shunt_VSS.anatomy: CSF drained from ventricle to superior sagittal sinus (same target anatomy as eShunt)
ventriculosinus_shunt_VSS.analogous_to_eshunt_because: IDENTICAL venous target anatomy (superior sagittal sinus). VSS is the direct historical predecessor of eShunt.

evidence.Toma_2010: current shunt systems are not ideal with high revision rates on long-term follow-up (PMID 20177727)
evidence.Gabay_2022: 4 of 7 patients underwent shunt revisions; 2 had distal VSS revisions (J Neurosurg Pediatrics 31(3):p238)
evidence.Elwatidy_2009: Ventriculo-sagittal sinus shunt malfunction — causes of (nsj.org.sa 14(2):172)
evidence.Li_2021: no thrombosis in the sagittal sinus, no infection, over drainage, intracranial hemorrhage, or subdural effusion (small series, AME apm.amegroups.org/article/view/73160)
evidence.Wang_2025: VSS shunt positive clinical effect in hydrocephalus with elevated protein CSF (PMC11895313)

ventriculosinus_shunt_VSS.epistemic_class: MIXED — historical VSS has high revision rates, but specific obstruction/thrombosis evidence is mixed. VSS is the SAME anatomy as eShunt, making this the most directly relevant analog.
ventriculosinus_shunt_VSS.key_limitation: Historical VSS used OPEN surgical placement with long catheters. eShunt uses ENDOVASCULAR placement with a short, direct implant. The delivery method and implant length differ, which may affect fouling mode.

venous_sinu_stenting_VSS_stent.anatomy: Stent placed in dural venous sinus for IIH/venous stenosis
venous_sinu_stenting_VSS_stent.analogous_to_eshunt_because: Both involve a foreign body implanted in the dural venous sinus. Both are at risk of sinus thrombosis.
venous_sinu_stenting_VSS_stent.evidence: Townsend 2021 (PMC8722449) — delayed stent thrombosis is a documented complication requiring revascularization
venous_sinu_stenting_VSS_stent.epistemic_class: INDEPENDENT_PEER_REVIEWED — confirms that foreign bodies in the dural venous sinus can thrombose

prindeze_2024.finding: Development of an in vitro ventricular shunt material testing... The application of antifouling surfaces to ventricular shunts shows considerable promise for improving efficacy.
prindeze_2024.epistemic_class: PEER_REVIEWED — confirms that anti-fouling surfaces for CSF shunts is an active research area
prindeze_2024.note: This is for VENTRICULAR shunts (VP), not eShunt specifically. But it confirms the fouling problem class is real for CSF shunts.

VP_shunt_evidence_EXPLICITLY_EXCLUDED.reason: CEO directive: 'Do not substitute generic VP-shunt obstruction evidence for eShunt evidence.' VP shunts have a long distal catheter in the peritoneum, which is anatomically different from eShunt's short venous-sinus implant. VP shunt obstruction modes (choroid plexus ingrowth into proximal catheter, omentum wrapping of distal catheter) are NOT transferable to eShunt.
VP_shunt_evidence_EXPLICITLY_EXCLUDED.vp_shunt_obstruction_rate: ~10-15% (well-documented in literature, but NOT admissible as eShunt evidence per CEO directive)

question_1_failure_mode_occurs.question: Does the eShunt fouling/obstruction failure mode actually occur?
question_1_failure_mode_occurs.answer: YELLOW — plausible but not yet observed in eShunt-specific clinical data
question_1_failure_mode_occurs.eshunt_specific_evidence: 0 device-related SAEs in ~30-100 patients across pilot + STRIDE trials, 90-day to 6-month follow-up. No obstruction events reported in any available eShunt clinical data.
question_1_failure_mode_occurs.anatomical_analogy_evidence: VA shunts (drain CSF to venous atrium) have 20% thrombosis at 2 years, up to 60% in autopsy series. VSS (drain CSF to superior sagittal sinus — SAME target as eShunt) has high revision rates. Venous sinus stents thrombose. All three anatomical analogs confirm venous-side CSF drainage / foreign-body-in-sinus has real thrombosis risk.
question_1_failure_mode_occurs.clinical_exposure_limitation: eShunt clinical exposure is limited (~30-100 patients, short follow-up). The device is investigational. Long-term patency data does not yet exist. Absence of observed obstruction is NOT evidence of absence (Article XXV).
question_1_failure_mode_occurs.verdict: PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNOBSERVED_IN_ESHUNT. The failure mode is biologically defensible based on anatomical analogy, but has not yet been observed in eShunt-specific clinical data. This is a YELLOW gate, not a GREEN gate.
question_1_failure_mode_occurs.implication: Any candidate mechanism must be framed as PREVENTIVE against a plausible-but-unobserved failure mode, not as a solution to an observed clinical problem. The value proposition is weaker than if the problem were clinically confirmed.

question_2_matters_to_buyer.question: Does the failure mode matter to the buyer (CereVasc)?
question_2_matters_to_buyer.answer: YES — conditional on the problem materializing
question_2_matters_to_buyer.evidence: CereVasc's own marketing positions eShunt as having REDUCED obstruction vs VP shunts. If eShunt develops a venous-side thrombosis/obstruction problem in long-term follow-up, it would undermine the core value proposition. VA shunt evidence shows venous-side thrombosis is SERIOUS (life-threatening, requires revision).
question_2_matters_to_buyer.verdict: BUYER_IMPACT_HIGH_CONDITIONAL. If the problem materializes at rates similar to VA shunts (20%+), it would be a clinically severe, commercially critical issue. But the problem has not materialized yet in eShunt.

question_3_mechanism_changes_physical_qu.question: Does the proposed mechanism change the relevant physical quantity?
question_3_mechanism_changes_physical_qu.answer: PENDING — depends on candidate mechanism. Not yet evaluated.
question_3_mechanism_changes_physical_qu.note: This question will be evaluated for each surviving candidate in Step 5.

question_4_change_large_enough.question: Is the change large enough to matter?
question_4_change_large_enough.note: This question will be evaluated for each surviving candidate in Step 7 (physics).

question_5_creates_larger_failure_mode.question: Does the intervention create a larger failure mode?
question_5_creates_larger_failure_mode.note: This question will be evaluated for each surviving candidate. This is especially important given CE-005's lesson: V7 FDVBZ's flow-direction approach introduced embolization risk (a LARGER failure mode).

overall_gate_verdict.verdict: YELLOW — PROCEED WITH CAUTION TO EXPLORATION PHASE
overall_gate_verdict.rationale: The eShunt fouling/obstruction problem is PLAUSIBLE based on anatomical analogy to VA shunts and VSS (both drain CSF to the venous system and both experience thrombosis), but has NOT been observed in eShunt-specific clinical data (limited exposure, short follow-up). Per Article XXXIII (no irreversible research action on unresolved evidence), the exploration phase (Steps 2-7) may proceed, but NO candidate will be promoted without (a) resolving the yellow state at Question 1, AND (b) passing Questions 3-5 for the specific candidate.
constraints_on_exploration: NO candidate will be promoted as a SOLUTION until Question 1 is resolved (either by longer eShunt follow-up data, or by accepting the anatomical analogy as sufficient).
ANY candidate must be framed as PREVENTIVE against a plausible-but-unobserved failure mode, with the weaker value proposition that entails.
The CEO's anti-rescue rule applies: V7 FDVBZ (flow-direction-dependent) stays dead. Reopening #5 is to discover a FUNDAMENTALLY DIFFERENT causal mechanism, not to rescue V7.
CE-005's reusable lesson applies: ANY flow-direction-dependent mechanism must be tested against retrograde flow robustness. Non-flow-direction mechanisms are NOT in CE-005's blast radius.

strongest_alternative_explanation_per_ar.alternative: The alternative explanation is that eShunt's short, direct, endovascular design INHERENTLY avoids the fouling/obstruction problem that plagues VP shunts (long catheter) and VA shunts (long catheter in atrium). On this view, eShunt may never develop a significant fouling problem, and #5 may be a non-problem.
strongest_alternative_explanation_per_ar.test: The STRIDE trial 5-year follow-up data will be decisive. If eShunt shows 0 obstruction events at 5 years in a larger cohort, the problem-existence gate FAILS and #5 closes permanently. If obstruction events appear, the gate turns GREEN and #5 becomes urgent.
strongest_alternative_explanation_per_ar.current_status: UNRESOLVED — cannot be decided without longer follow-up data. Exploration proceeds in parallel.
